days.theme: Arrive Wulingyuan, clear the East Gate, walk the valley floor
days.why: Train clears 12:45 at Zhangjiajie West, ~1 h transfer to Wulingyuan, so the park day realistically starts ~14:30 — about 3.5 h of stop time. The East Gate's 45 min is not a queue, it's the manual counter for passport + facial registration that ties the ticket to your passport; doing it today activates the 4-day pass and makes tomorrow's 07:00 re-entry fast. Golden Whip Stream is the only thing that survives a late train: flat, shaded, no cableway, no timed slot, no queue. Shuttle from East Gate to Shuiraosimen and walk it downstream toward the Forest Park gate. Nothing requiring a lift or a cable car can start this late. Golden Whip Stream is CAPPED at 19:00 and gets 2h03 of its 2h45 advice. The binding constraint is the last eco-shuttle out, not a gate — the trail is a 7.5 km unlit gorge and the chain had you finishing at 19:42, after sunset, deep in the valley. This is exactly the fallback this day already anticipated: walk part-way and turn back to Shuiraosimen rather than committing to the full length. Confidence on that 19:00 is LOW; confirm the last shuttle when you buy the park ticket.

days.theme: Wulingyuan plateau — Bailong up, Avatar peaks, Tianzi, cable car down
days.why: 9 h of stop time — the day the whole city exists for. The order is dictated by the mountain, not by preference: you can only ascend at Bailong, traverse the plateau north to Tianzi by shuttle (~40 min), then descend, and the Tianzi cableway lands in the Shili valley where Ten-Mile Gallery starts, so it is free to add. Be at the East Gate for 07:00 opening: the Bailong queue is 1–2 h from mid-morning in August and the 60 min budgeted here only holds if you are early. Tianzi cableway's last car is ~17:30, which the sequence clears by roughly 90 min. Yangjiajie was cut here — it hangs off the far west of the plateau and costs its own cableway plus ~1 h of extra shuttling, which would push this day past 13 h. Breakfast to 06:30 and lunch to 11:30. The early start is what pulls Ten-Mile Gallery out of the dark: on a 07:00 start it ran 20:19-21:49, well after both sunset and the last tram, on a stop whose whole point is the valley floor at the foot of the Tianzi descent. It now runs 17:33-19:03. Lunch is held to 11:30 so it lands straight off Yuanjiajie — the default noon window fired it after Tianzi instead, which meant climbing 2.5 h on an empty stomach and eating at 14:38.

days.theme: Tianmen Mountain — day trip to Zhangjiajie city
days.why: Separate park, ~40 km away above the city — it cannot share a day with Wulingyuan, and at 4–5 h on the summit plus the transfer it fills one. 6 h of stop time plus ~2.5 h of intercity bus makes a full but tapered day before the early departure. Leave the hotel ~06:15 for the first bus: the mountain runs nine timed slots 07:00–16:00, and the difference between the 07:00 slot and an afternoon one is 0–15 min of queue versus 90–120 min. With the cableway's upper section shut until 2027, Line C is the clean version — shuttle from downtown to the Tianmen Cave gate, then the express cableway up and back the same way, which is why the transport block is 75 min rather than a simple lift ride. Two data corrections. The Tianmen cableway is the ASCENT, not a stop 27 km from the mountain — the router was charging a 51-minute road trip around the massif between the cableway and the summit it delivers you to; that leg is now zero, and the 75-min cableway dwell carries the shuttle, the ride and its peak queue. And the run down to Zhangjiajie city was being measured from breakfast rather than the hotel, so 28 km read as a 22-minute walk; it is 48 minutes. Lunch at 15:07 is late and deliberate: Tianmen is a single 4h15 block and you come straight down into it — carry something for the summit.

Station by 08:30 for a 09:15 train, and Zhangjiajie West is ~1 h from Wulingyuan, so you are leaving the hotel around 07:30. There is no sight in either park that opens early enough or sits close enough to fit. Breakfast and go.

ideas.name: Yangjiajie cableway
ideas.why: The lift that makes Yangjiajie reachable — cut with the area it serves. Only worth restoring if you add a fifth day or trade away the entire Tianzi/Ten-Mile half of day 2.

ideas.name: Yangjiajie
ideas.why: Genuinely excellent and much quieter than Yuanjiajie — Natural Great Wall and One Step to Heaven — but it sits at the far western end of the plateau. Reaching it costs its own cable car plus roughly an hour of extra shuttle each way, about 4 h of marginal cost against Ten-Mile Gallery's 90 min for zero extra transfer. With one afternoon and two full days it is the correct thing to lose. If you would rather have it than Tianmen, swap the whole of day 3 for it — do not try to squeeze it into day 2.

notes: Ranking: MUST = Yuanjiajie (Avatar), Tianzi Mountain, Bailong Elevator, Tianmen Mountain, Wulingyuan East Gate, and the two transport legs that are the only way up/down (Tianzi cableway down, Tianmen cableway). WORTH = Golden Whip Stream (perfect arrival-afternoon filler), Ten-Mile Gallery (free rider at the foot of the Tianzi descent), Bus to Zhangjiajie city (enabler). DROP = Yangjiajie + its cableway.

One park per day is not a preference, it is geography: Wulingyuan (Avatar peaks) and Tianmen Mountain (above Zhangjiajie city) are ~35–45 km apart. The old plan's day 3 — Yangjiajie in the morning then Tianmen in the afternoon — cannot physically happen, and an afternoon Tianmen arrival also collides with the 16:00 last timed slot and the worst queues of the day.

Tianmen's main cableway upper section (mid-station to summit) closed 6 Nov 2025 for a multi-year rebuild, expected to reopen 2027. Line C avoids it entirely. Line A is the scenic alternative at the same price — downtown cableway to the mid-station, eco-bus up the 99 Bends to Tianmen Cave, escalators to the summit, walk DOWN the 999 steps — but it runs ~1 h longer and is a bigger commitment from a Wulingyuan base. Book whichever you pick for the earliest slot.

Book both parks in advance against your passport numbers. The Wulingyuan ticket (~¥240) is multi-day and covers the free eco-shuttles, so day 1 and day 2 are one purchase; Tianmen is a separate timed-entry ticket for a fixed date.

Day 2 is ~9 h of stop time plus roughly 2 h of intra-park shuttle — about 11 h door to door. That is what a Wulingyuan plateau day costs in August; the queue time is already inside the stop durations. Do not add anything to it.

Day 1 fallback: if the 12:30 train slips, walk Golden Whip Stream part-way and turn back to Shuiraosimen for the shuttle instead of committing to the full 7.5 km to the Forest Park gate. It is the one stop on the whole city that shortens cleanly.

'Check in at Yuji Hotel' is left out of stops per the no-hotels rule, but it still needs ~25 min on day 1 between the transfer from Zhangjiajie West and the East Gate — the hotel is 1.5 km from the sign gate, so bag-drop first then walk over.
'Bus to Zhangjiajie city' on day 3 is a there-and-back day trip, not a checkout — you sleep in Wulingyuan all three nights, so leave your luggage at the hotel.
